title: 工作太多赶不上，怎么和经理协商优先级？
topic: 用工作量、截止时间和优先级说明需要调整的安排

source.title: Sustainable High Performance at Octopus
source.type: 公开员工手册（工作与健康边界）
source.context: Octopus Deploy 的真实工作材料，本课练习聚焦一个常见职场沟通任务。

translations: 设定适合自己时区和个人生活的工作时间，并坚持执行。让团队了解你的工作节奏。
倦怠很少会自行消失。如果你接近承受极限，就和经理谈谈。我们宁愿调整优先级，也不愿让你的健康受到影响。

fullTextParagraphs: Protecting energy, focus, and wellbeing—so Octonauts can thrive, not just perform.

At Octopus, we’re proud to be a remote-first company with team members distributed across 17 countries and multiple time zones. This global, flexible way of working presents us with incredible opportunities, but it also poses challenges. One of them is maintaining healthy boundaries and preventing burnout in a world where work and home often occupy the same physical space.

Work-life balance isn’t just a talking point for us. It’s foundational to how we believe great work gets done. Our culture emphasizes outcomes over hours worked, and we trust every Octonaut to manage their energy, focus, and well-being with the same care they apply to their work. That’s why it is built into our company’s values, “Doing a smaller number of things at high quality.” This autonomy is powerful, but it also comes with responsibility.

As a global, home-based team, it’s easy for meetings to encroach on personal time, or for work to spill into evenings and weekends. And because we’re all driven by meaningful work, we sometimes blur the line between passion and overcommitment.
That’s why it’s crucial that we remain vigilant, for ourselves and for one another.
Burnout doesn’t always show up as low performance. In fact, high-performing, highly engaged people are often the most at risk. Be alert for these patterns in yourself or your teammates:
Working longer hours consistently, with little recovery time
Feeling like you’re constantly falling behind despite working more
Cancelling personal plans or skipping breaks to “catch up”
Losing interest in projects that used to excite you
Becoming more irritable, reactive, or withdrawn
Struggling with sleep or mental fatigue
Increasing mistakes, delays, or attention gaps
Disengaging from team rituals or collaboration

At Octopus, we want you to pay attention to them early on. We want you to do good work, but not at the expense of your mental and physical health. That’s why we’re guided by our values that support sustainable human-centered work:
Listening to our customers, over following market trends. We show up fully for customers by showing up fully for ourselves and each other.
Helping each other, over being efficient individual contributors. We’re stronger together. Burnout isolates; support connects.
Doing the right thing by our customers & team, over short-term gain. Slowing down to protect well-being is often the most strategic move.
Doing a smaller number of things at high quality, over trying to do everything or hitting arbitrary deadlines. Focus and depth beat quantity and haste—always.
A bias for action, over risk aversion, or the pursuit of the perfect plan. Taking action includes speaking up when you’re not okay. It’s courageous, not weak.
Clear Boundaries Set working hours that suit your time zone and personal life, and stick to them. Let your team know your rhythm.
Meeting Discipline We encourage teams to regularly audit their meetings. If something can be async, make it async. If a meeting rotates time zones, share the load.
Time Off is Sacred Use your leave and when you’re off, truly disconnect by ensuring a handover plan is in place. Breaks are important for sustainable performance, not a pause from it.
Speak Up Early Burnout rarely resolves on its own. If you’re nearing a limit, talk to your manager. We’d rather shift priorities than risk your health.
Support Each Other Look out for signs in your teammates. A quick check-in, a kind question, or a nudge to take a break can make a big difference.
Leaders Set the Tone If you lead a team, model healthy work patterns. Create space for honest conversations about workload, energy, and capacity. What you do matters more than what you say.

Preventing burnout isn’t about doing less; it’s about working in a way that’s sustainable, focused, and human. We want you to thrive at Octopus, and thriving means taking care of yourself first. It’s not a side project, it’s part of the job. And remember, you’re not in this alone. If you ever feel unsure, overwhelmed, or running on empty, reach out. We’re here to help because doing the right thing by our team starts with listening and showing up for each other.

notes.phrase: Set working hours that suit your time zone and personal life, and stick to them.
notes.meaning: 设定适合自己时区和生活的工作时间，并遵守安排。
notes.explain: suit your time zone and personal life 说明安排工作时间时要考虑个人现实。
notes.example: Let’s agree on working hours that suit both time zones.

notes.phrase: If you’re nearing a limit, talk to your manager. We’d rather shift priorities than risk your health.
notes.meaning: 如果你接近承受极限，就和经理谈谈。我们宁愿调整优先级，也不愿让你的健康受到影响。
notes.explain: shift priorities 表示调整任务先后顺序。
notes.example: Could we shift priorities so I can finish the client proposal first?

notes.phrase: Create space for honest conversations about workload, energy, and capacity.
notes.meaning: 为坦诚讨论工作量、精力和承载能力留出空间。
notes.explain: workload、energy 和 capacity 分别涉及任务量、精力和可承接量。
notes.example: Let’s discuss workload and capacity before adding another project.

scenario.title: 模拟情境：两个重要项目撞上同一截止日
english: You are preparing a customer proposal and a product update for the same Friday deadline.
Both tasks need review, and the current workload makes it unlikely that both will be ready on time.
Explain the capacity issue, recommend which task to prioritize, and ask your manager to confirm the order.
chinese: 你要准备一份客户方案和一份产品更新，两项都要求周五完成。
两项工作都需要审核，按目前工作量很难按时完成。
请说明时间压力，建议优先完成哪一项，并请经理确认顺序。

firstAttempt.prompt: 客户方案和产品更新都要求周五完成，但你没有足够时间保证两项都按时交付。请用英语说明工作量，提出优先顺序，并请经理确认。
firstAttempt.sample: I’m concerned that I won’t be able to finish both the customer proposal and the product update by Friday. Could we shift priorities and complete the customer proposal first? I can send the product update on Monday, if that works for the team. Please let me know which deadline should take priority.
firstAttempt.rationale: 说明当前容量问题，提出先后顺序和替代时间，再让经理确认安排。

words.example: I’d like to discuss my workload before taking on another project.
words.translation: 在接手另一个项目之前，我想先讨论一下工作量。
words.note: 可用于说明手上工作总量。

words.example: My current capacity allows me to complete one priority task this week.
words.translation: 我本周的可用时间只能完成一项优先任务。
words.note: 用于沟通当前能承接多少工作。

words.collocation: shift priorities to meet a deadline
words.example: We may need to shift priorities to meet the client deadline.
words.translation: 我们可能需要调整优先顺序，以赶上客户截止时间。
words.note: 用于重新安排任务，而不是一味加速。

taskPhrases.word: I’m concerned that I won’t be able to finish both by Friday
taskPhrases.meaning: 我担心周五前无法完成这两项工作
taskPhrases.example: I’m concerned that I won’t be able to finish both drafts by Friday.
taskPhrases.translation: 我担心周五前无法完成两份草稿。

taskPhrases.word: Could we shift priorities and complete A first?
taskPhrases.meaning: 我们能调整优先顺序，先完成 A 吗？
taskPhrases.collocation: Could we shift priorities and + verb?
taskPhrases.example: Could we shift priorities and complete the client proposal first?
taskPhrases.translation: 我们能调整优先顺序，先完成客户方案吗？

taskPhrases.word: Please let me know which deadline should take priority
taskPhrases.meaning: 请告诉我哪个截止时间应该优先
taskPhrases.example: Please let me know which task should take priority.
taskPhrases.translation: 请告诉我哪项任务应该优先。

structure.original: We’d rather shift priorities than risk your health.
analysis: would rather A than B 表示宁愿做 A，也不愿承担 B 的后果。
shift priorities 是可执行的替代办法。
讨论工作量时，可以同时提出自己建议的顺序和交付时间。
structure.transfer: We’d rather move the launch date than release the customer update without review.

rewrite.bad: I have too much work. I can’t do this.
rewrite.good: I’m concerned that I won’t be able to finish both the customer proposal and the product update by Friday. Could we shift priorities and complete the customer proposal first? I can send the product update on Monday, if that works for the team. Please let me know which deadline should take priority.
rewrite.translation: 我担心周五前无法完成客户方案和产品更新。我们能调整优先顺序，先完成客户方案吗？如果团队可以，我周一提交产品更新。请告诉我哪个截止时间应该优先。
rewrite.pattern: I’m concerned that I can’t complete [A] and [B] by [date]. Could we prioritize [A]? I can deliver [B] by [new date].

choice.prompt: 你手上有两个周五截止的任务，但只能按时完成一项。哪种做法最有帮助？
options: Say “I’m too busy” without explaining the tasks or proposing a plan.
Explain the capacity limit, recommend the task to prioritize, and ask the manager to confirm the order.
Work late without discussing the risk, then miss both deadlines.
choice.why: 第二种说明了工作量、给出顺序建议并请经理确认，便于团队及时调整计划。

output.prompt: 经理临时加了一份周五要交的客户培训材料。你还负责周五到期的客户方案和产品更新，三项工作无法都按时完成。请说明工作量，建议先完成客户方案、把产品更新改到周一，并请经理确认培训材料的优先顺序。
output.sample: I’m concerned that I won’t be able to finish the proposal, product update, and training materials by Friday. Could we prioritize the customer proposal and move the product update to Monday? Please let me know whether the training materials should take priority over one of the other deadlines.
check: 说明三项任务都在周五到期
提出优先完成的任务和新交付时间
请经理确认剩余工作的先后顺序
